basis: Every model-emitted ontology identifier in pots-findings v1.1 flagged ontology_id_verification=unverified_model_emitted (16,662 rows; 6,120 distinct entity-name x id pairs; HGNC 9,661 rows, ChEBI 4,880, MeSH 2,116, GO 4, HP 1) was looked up BY ID at its minting authority (MyGene/HGNC, OLS4 ChEBI, NLM MeSH) and the authority's label + full synonym/alias list compared to the entity name; forward resolution (name -> id) was also run to obtain the repair candidate. 2026-10-21; HTTP only, no model in the loop.
reading: Model-emitted identifiers virtually always EXIST (99.98%) but about a third denote a different entity — typically a neighbouring gene (SCN9A -> SCN8A's id), a related compound (naltrexone -> naloxone), or a sibling concept. Existence checks therefore catch nothing; only label correspondence does. About 65% of the flagged ids were in fact correct, so nulling them wholesale would have discarded ~10,800 usable identifiers; retrospective verification keeps those as authority-verified and repairs or nulls the rest.
caveats: 'denotes_one_of_compound_name' = the entity string lists several entities and the id denotes one of them (3.9%): partially correct
relaxed matching tolerates case, plural, Greek letters, punctuation and parentheticals; it does not use string similarity for acceptance
MeSH lookups used descriptor details; supplementary-concept ids (C-prefix) have fewer synonyms, so MeSH 'wrong' may be slightly overstated
